\begin{example} \end{example}[hyperbolas on hyperbolic space]

Source: petersen:page-0192 ↗ def:pet-ch5-geodesic ↗ prop:pet-ch5-mixed-partials-submanifold 1. ch5:5.2.10On $H^n(R)\subset \mathbb R^{n,1}$, the acceleration is again the Minkowski projection of the ambient (Euclidean-formula) acceleration, and $T_pH^n(R)=\{ v\mid v\perp p\} $ in the Minkowski sense. The curves $c(t)=p\cosh (at)+v\sinh (at)$, $p,v\in \mathbb R^{n,1}$, $|p|^2=-R^2$, $|v|^2=R^2$, $p\perp v$ (Minkowski), satisfy $\ddot c=a^2c$, proportional to $c$ hence normal to $H^n(R)$, so these hyperbolas are the geodesics. \end{example}
